def: The PCIe packet that carries a request (memory read or write, configuration, message) or a completion between two PCIe components.
A ring of 64-byte command entries in host memory. The host writes commands at the tail and rings the SQ tail doorbell; the controller fetches entries from the head.
A ring of 16-byte completion entries in host memory. The controller writes entries at its tail with the current phase tag; the host consumes them and reports progress with the CQ head doorbell.
A controller register in BAR0 (from offset 1000h) that the host writes to publish a new SQ tail or a new CQ head. A doorbell write is a posted PCIe Memory Write; it carries an index, not a command.
The Linux kernel structure describing one block I/O: target device and sector, operation and flags, and a list of memory segments. blk-mq turns bios into requests for the driver.
The Linux block layer design that keeps per-CPU software queues and maps them to hardware queues; it allocates the request tag from which the NVMe driver derives the Command Identifier.
An address that a device uses for DMA when an IOMMU is enabled. The IOMMU translates it to a physical address; addresses seen on the PCIe link (PRPs, queue bases) are IOVAs.
SSD firmware that maps logical block addresses to physical flash locations, performs out-of-place writes, garbage collection and wear leveling. Invisible on the PCIe link.
Field in CQE DW2 (bits 15:0) reporting how far the controller has consumed the submission queue named by the SQ Identifier, so the host knows which SQ slots are free.
Bit 16 of CQE DW3. The controller inverts the value it writes each time it wraps the completion queue, so the host can tell new entries from old ones without a separate valid bit.
Bit 30 of CDW12 in Read and Write commands. On a write, the controller must place the data on non-volatile media before completing the command.
A controller write cache whose contents can be lost on power failure. Reported in Identify Controller and controlled through the Volatile Write Cache feature; durability then needs FUA or Flush.
SSD hardware (typically capacitors) and firmware that finish writing cached data to flash after power fails. Drives with PLP usually report no volatile write cache.
PCIe Device Control field limiting how many bytes one Memory Read request may ask for. A device pulling WRITE data splits its reads accordingly.
The address alignment (64 or 128 bytes) at which a completer may split the completions for one read request.
Completion header field giving the number of bytes still to be returned for the read request, including the current completion; equal to the payload length on the last completion.

Field chosen by a requester to identify one outstanding non-posted request; with the Requester ID it forms the Transaction ID used to match completions. Reused as soon as the request completes; unrelated to the NVMe Command Identifier.
16-bit value in SQE CDW0 bits 31:16, chosen by the host. Unique among outstanding commands of one submission queue; returned in the CQE so the host can match completion to command.
Requester ID plus Tag: the PCIe identifier that must be unique among a requester's outstanding non-posted requests and that routes and matches their completions.
Course term: the field (address, slot index, tag, SQID plus CID, vector) that links one stage of an NVMe command's trail on the PCIe link to the next, valid within a scope and for a lifetime.

Course term for a trace event that cannot be attributed to any outstanding request or command: a completion with no request, data outside every PRP range, a CQE with no outstanding command. Orphans usually point at the bug.
